Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for returning the SIG. Our InfoSec team had a few follow-up items specifically around data retention and whether customer inputs are used to train models or stored long-term:

1) Can you confirm the retention windows for prompt logs vs. audit logs? We need exact defaults and whether those can be shortened.
2) We asked about KV cache — is that persisted to disk or retained beyond a session? If so, what are the retention controls?
3) Do you ever use customer prompts or responses to train Redwood models by default? If yes, what controls are in place for opt-out?
4) Please provide any artifacts (policy, SOC2, architecture diagram) we can attach to our procurement package.

We'd appreciate concise answers and any evidence we can include. If you prefer to call, we can set up a 30-min sync next week.

Best,
Sara Miller
Security Lead, Medica Health

Medica Health | security-requests@medicahealth.com
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers and attached evidence. Happy to expand on any line.

1) Prompt logs vs audit logs:
- Prompt logs (request/response pairs used to serve API calls) are ephemeral by default and retained for 30 days in the hosted product. These logs are used for troubleshooting, rate-limiting analysis, and abuse detection. Customers may request shorter retention windows via their account team; we can support retention as low as 0 days (ephemeral) by configuration for enterprise plans.
- Audit logs (administrative actions, access events, billing records) are stored separately in an append-only audit store. Default retention is 365 days for hosted customers; enterprise customers can request extended retention (multi-year) in the contract.

2) KV cache persistence:
- The KV cache (per-request attention cache) lives in-memory on inference nodes and is flushed when sessions end or instances are recycled. We do not persist per-customer KV caches to durable disk by default. For Dedicated/Private deployments, operators can configure local disk persistence for performance, but that is disabled in our hosted offering. Please see attached "kv-cache-architecture-diagram.png" for the in-memory flow and eviction policy.

3) Training on customer data:
- Redwood does NOT use customer prompt or response data to train or improve our base models by default for hosted customers. Any model training that uses customer data requires an explicit opt-in and a signed agreement (data use addendum). For Dedicated and Private deployments, customer data remains under customer control and is never used to train our models.

4) Evidence artifacts attached:
- retention-policy-2026-09.pdf (policy excerpt with configurable windows)
- redwood-data-usage-attestation.txt (explicit attestation about training and opt-in controls)
- soc2-redwood-2025-type2.pdf (recent SOC2 Type II report redacted)
- kv-cache-architecture-diagram.png
- completed SIG exhibit: sig-completed-exhibit.pdf

Notes on controls: all persisted data is encrypted at rest with customer keys (where provided) via KMS. In-transit encryption uses TLS 1.2+/mTLS for private links. Access to logs is restricted via RBAC and audited; we can provide an access matrix on request.

If you want, we can produce a short two-page summary for procurement that extracts the lines above and lists the attachments. Would next Wednesday at 10:00 AM PT work for a 30-min review?

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Sara — quick technical addendum from our security team:

- Logging pipeline: prompt logs are written to a short-lived blob store with TTL enforcement; a separate, immutable audit stream (Kafka + cold storage) captures admin events. Both streams are encrypted at rest (AES-256) and keys are rotated quarterly.
- KMS/HSM: we integrate with customer-managed KMS for enterprise customers; HSM-backed signing for audit events is available for Dedicated customers.
- Deletion & compliance: delete requests are honored within 72 hours for hosted customers; we provide deletion evidence (audit trail and purge confirmation). For legal hold or regulatory requirements, retention can be extended with written justification and contractual terms.
- Access controls: engineers do not have blanket access to customer prompt streams; access requests go through an approval workflow and are logged in our SIEM.

I uploaded a small folder with the architecture diagram and a short data-flow readme to our shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-medica-evidence.

If you want more technical artifacts (trace logs, anonymized event samples), let me know what scope and we can package them.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
